subject: Unit economics follow-up: token volumes, budget range, and $/1M tokens target
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps — unit economics & pricing qualification

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's call and a couple of asks to help us model a tailored pricing/POC: 

1) Expected monthly token volumes (approx): you mentioned 20M–50M generated tokens initially and potential to scale to ~250M over 12 months. Please confirm if those are per month or total for first 6 months.
2) Feature set: we discussed 3 key features to start — Conversational assistant (FAQ + routing), document summarization (internal ops), and personalized recommendations. If you can rank these by revenue impact that helps our $/feature modelling.
3) Budget/buying intent: you mentioned a preliminary budget range of $80k–$150k/mo for inference and platform (inclusive of support). Confirm if that should include reserved capacity or pure hosted usage.

Attached I’m sending a short unit economics deck and an editable pricing model where we can plug your exact volume mix. High-level things we'll model on our side: $/1M tokens at different tiers, expected inference cost per 1M tokens (GPU + overhead), margin targets per feature, and CAC payback assumptions for a pilot-to-paid conversion.

Next steps I propose:
- You: confirm token volume cadence (monthly vs cumulative) and rank features by value — reply to this thread.
- Me: I’ll run the model and send a recommended pricing band + a canary POC plan by EOD Friday.

Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_unit_econ_presentation_v3.pdf (17 slides), pricing_model_v2.xlsx (editable), sample_malp_token_analysis.csv (token mix sample)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps — unit economics & pricing qualification

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: the 20M–50M was expected monthly for month 1–3 across our US user base. The 250M figure is monthly target by month 12 if expansion goes well.
- Feature priority: 1) Conversational assistant (primary), 2) Personalized recommendations, 3) Document summarization (internal ops — lower priority for revenue).
- Budget: our procurement gave a flexible range initially — $80k–$150k/mo. We are open to reserved capacity if it reduces unit costs materially, but we need to keep flexibility until M3.

Two technical notes that will affect costing: token mix — we expect a high prompt:completion ratio (roughly 2.8 prompts : 1 completion token on average) because we send contextual history + metadata. Also, 40% of calls will be short (<50 tokens) and 20% will be long (>=1024 tokens).

Can you include an expected $/1M tokens number for both hosted and reserved (dedicated) scenarios and a suggested target price we should aim for (e.g., $X per 1M tokens) to meet our margin goals (we’re targeting 30–40% gross margin on features tied to inference cost)?

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up next week if that’s easier.

—Alex
VP Product, FinTechX
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps — unit economics & pricing qualification

Alex — thanks, super helpful detail. I ran a first-pass unit economics model (attaching the editable sheet). Key outputs and assumptions below — calling these out explicitly so we’re aligned: 

Assumptions (please flag if any look off):
- Token mix: prompt:completion 2.8:1 overall; short calls (40%) avg total tokens 40; long calls (20%) avg total tokens 1,200; remaining 40% mid-length ~300 tokens.
- Inference cost breakdown (hosted): GPU amortized + runtime + I/O = $6.50 per 1M tokens at baseline (current open model variant we discussed).
- Inference cost breakdown (reserved/dedicated): with committed capacity and optimized kernels we estimate $3.25 per 1M tokens at scale (250M+ monthly with autoscaling & batching). This assumes quantization and 8-bit kernels where applicable.
- Redwood platform fee + support (baseline for hosted): add $2.50 per 1M tokens. For reserved we typically price platform fee as a flat monthly seat/reserved fee — for modelling I’m adding $1.10 per 1M tokens equivalent at your 250M target.

Resulting $/1M tokens (net to you) — first-pass: 
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): ~$9.00 per 1M tokens (6.50 infra + 2.50 platform)
- Reserved (committed, 250M+): ~$4.35 per 1M tokens (3.25 infra + 1.10 platform)

What that implies for your margin/feature math (assuming you target 30–40% gross margin on features where inference is the primary cost):
- If your feature sells at $X per 1M tokens consumed by customers, to achieve 35% gross margin you need: X such that (X - inference_cost) / X = 0.35 => X = inference_cost / (1 - 0.35).
- Plug numbers: Hosted target price ≈ $13.85 per 1M tokens to hit 35% margin. Reserved target price ≈ $6.69 per 1M tokens to hit 35% margin.

$/feature and CAC payback examples (quick scenarios):
- Conversational assistant: average revenue per active user/month = $2.50; average tokens consumed per active user/month = 6k tokens => inference cost per user (hosted) = (6k / 1,000,000) * $9.00 = $0.054; margin per user ~ $2.446 => inference is small as a percent. CAC payback: if CAC = $45, payback on gross margin = 45 / 2.446 ≈ 18.4 months (long — implies need to either reduce CAC or increase ARPU or target reserved pricing).
- Recommendation API (inference-heavy): avg rev per user/month = $4.00; tokens/user/month = 120k => inference cost (hosted) = 0.12 * $9.00 = $1.08; margin per user = $2.92; CAC payback @ $45 = 15.4 months. Reserved pricing reduces inference cost to ~0.12 * $4.35 = $0.522 => payback reduces to ~11.2 months.

Notes & recommendations:
- If you need to hit 12-month CAC payback across these features, reserved capacity materially helps and is the lever to push. At 250M+ committed volume we can structure pricing to get effective $/1M close to $4–5.
- We can also provide a hybrid approach: start hosted for months 1–3 with a conversion trigger to reserved once you hit the 120–150M mo threshold. We’ll model break-even points in the spreadsheet.

Attached: redwood_unit_econ_presentation_v3.pdf (narrative), pricing_model_v2.xlsx (editable assumptions — see "Volume Scenarios" tab), sample_malp_token_analysis.csv (token mix used).

If this looks good I’ll prepare:
- Formal pricing bands (hosted vs reserved) and a 90-day POC SOW with canaries and success metrics.
- Suggested contract language for conversion triggers and capacity commitment windows.

Would you be up for a 30-min follow-up Thursday to walk through the model and confirm the conversion trigger?

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_unit_econ_presentation_v3.pdf, pricing_model_v2.xlsx

Subject: Internal: next steps for FinTechX pricing offer

Quick internal note: Alex confirmed volumes and feature priority — they’re live-in-3 plan with 20M–50M/mo ramp to 250M/mo Y12. They’re targeting 30–40% gross margin on features. Action items: 

- Rachel: draft two pricing bands by EOD today (Hosted band + Reserved band at 250M commitment). Use the model in pricing_model_v2.xlsx. Show per-1M token math and suggested $/feature examples for Conversational assistant and Recommendation API.
- Neha: prepare a reserved capacity SOW template and convert-trigger clause (we should propose conversion at sustained 120M/month for 2 consecutive months). Also model how credits/overage will work in Q1.
- Me: set up Thurs 30-min demo with Alex + Samantha to walk model; include PM and infra SME.

Keep notes inline in the sheet. I’ll lead negotiations once we have the bands.

—Marissa
